_about: The words the box uses for a person: the glossary (docs/user/glossary.md is made from it: python3 tests/terms_guard.py --write), and the words to avoid in what a person reads. tests/terms_guard.py checks the messages (M(...) in irate_box/), the guide's sources and the pages' text against it. A pattern is a Python regular expression, matched without regard to case.

terms.definition: Who can open an app or page: Guests, Users, Administrators or Disabled
A user or administrator account that can sign in
An extra that an administrator can add or remove: Kiwix, Notes, Syncthing and others
A person with an administrator account. An administrator can change the box settings
The icon, the label and the size of a tile, and the colours of the hub
An offline reference in the ZIM format. Kiwix reads it
A local copy of a downloaded file that the box keeps
Throw away changes that you did not save
A page that checks one part of the box, lists the problems and offers repairs
A visitor without an account
The WiFi network of the box
Limits what devices on the hotspot can reach on the box. It does not filter the home network
The front page of the box and the program behind it
The state of a new box before an administrator account exists. Until an administrator creates the account, anyone on the network can open the administration pages
Put a downloaded package or add-on into use
A copy of a repository from another server, kept on the box
The repairs of the network watchdog, from the lightest to the heaviest (also called the ladder)
The time that the box keeps an item before it deletes it
Keep the changes that you made
Open a session with your account
The largest amount of storage that an item can use
A set of packages for one kind of job. Install it without internet if all its packages are in the cache
New versions of the box, apps, books and packages
A signed-in person who has an account
Shared files, drawings, posts and repositories
Who can see a tile on the hub

avoid.why: writing.md, Words; /admin as a path is fine
STE: let, not allow or permit

avoid.use: away from home, or say how (over Tailscale)
avoid.why: plain words: an old word for far away
